blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The proposed public-private partnership (PPP) aimed at modernizing and sustaining the country’s fuel marking program (FMP) has advanced after securing P19.16 million in technical and transaction advisory support. The provisional approval by the Project Development and Monitoring Facility (PDMF) committee was made during its sessions on July 12 and Aug. 12. The move is part of the government’s initiatives to combat illegal petroleum smuggling and fuel tax leakage. “The proposed modernization is an opportunity to strengthen the operational and technical capabilities supporting fuel marking and enforcement,” Glenn Sanchez Jr., head of operations at SICPA Philippines, said in a […]...
